title: Korean Army unveils robot-led battle drills for 2040 warfare
key_facts: The South Korean Army opened its Army TIGER+ integrated future-combat exercise to the media on 14 Oct 2026 at a range in Yangpyeong, Gyeonggi Province.
Drones, an anti-aircraft laser weapon and anti-drone systems worked alongside tanks and mortars in a simulated assault.
Unmanned reconnaissance vehicles, the K-CEV combat engineering vehicle, reconnaissance drones and four-legged robots entered a simulated minefield ahead of troops.
Army TIGER+ is the Army's plan to convert units to manned-unmanned teaming formations, applied across all units by 2040.
The goal responds to a shrinking pool of conscripts, shifting from troop numbers to unmanned assets.
